<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **40** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/presented-invitation.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-type-decision-tree.mdx`  _(via email_verified (literal, a string literal in invitationSignUpAwaitsVerification))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class), email_verified (literal, a string literal in invitationSignUpAwaitsVerification))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`  _(via email_verified (literal, a string literal in invitationSignUpAwaitsVerification))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/presented-invitation.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 56 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f27946cc9e6f5de5c86e8722fbb7b176c221e8ed` — the merge of head `bf3bf857d6d24772ef81266b807544ac61df771f` into base `d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f27946cc9e6f5de5c86e8722fbb7b176c221e8ed && git checkout f27946cc9e6f5de5c86e8722fbb7b176c221e8ed
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6 bf3bf857d6d24772ef81266b807544ac61df771f && git checkout -B drift-repro d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6 && git merge --no-ff bf3bf857d6d24772ef81266b807544ac61df771f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The seat adopts the delta record below. It was rendered on this head, at the contract-review tier, by the same isolated reviewer that recorded the earlier FAIL. The seat holds that FAIL record privately; mechanism detail stays with the security seat. This record is also the seat's confirmation of the DELIBERATE CORRECTION, judged sentence by sentence below.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bf3bf857d6d24772ef81266b807544ac61df771f`
Local-runs: probe — one throwaway worktree at `bf3bf857d6` (since removed; the shared clone was untouched) to verify the sync merge, the rule files and the ablations; what it ran:
- the sync-only check (merge-tree equals the head's tree; same net patch-id at `5147ad6a3a` and `bf3bf857d6`);
- four rule files, 65 passed;
- request-scope ablation: 1 of 30 red, exactly control (b);
- binding-rule ablation: 5 of 30 red;
- `check-empty-changeset` refuses only the corrected note;
- `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` exit 0.

The full suites, type check, derived gates, dogfood and CI were not run by the reviewer.

Scope: delta `48e427708a..5147ad6a3a` over the PR's net files, the sync merge to `bf3bf857d6`, and the replacement PR body.

### ① Derived judgments

**Earlier findings**

- **M1:** closed. See the DELIBERATE CORRECTION table below.
- **S1:** closed. The admission is held per creating request (`auth-manager.ts:3431-3454`, `auth-manager-membership-admission.ts:129-148`, `auth-manager-database-hooks.ts:281, 495-515`). No other creation of the same address reads it.
- **S3:** closed. Controls (a) and (b) at `invitation-acceptance-verified-address.test.ts:465-501`.
- **S4:** closed. `self-hosting.mdx:780-788` and the changeset carry the provider-verified exception.
- **N1:** closed. `invitationSignUpJoin.ts:104-113` routes straight to the verification prompt; pinned.
- **N3:** closed. The proof control now distinguishes a bind at creation plus acceptance.
- **N4:** closed.
- **S2:** deferred to follow-up card #34889. Accepted.
- **N2:** outside the diff; it stays a nit.

**DELIBERATE CORRECTION: `.changeset/34272-accept-invitation-verified-email.md`**

The PR body's table matches the diff row for row.

| Part | Before, at this head | After, at this head |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Summary line | False: "while mail is live" is no longer a condition. | True |
| `Clause-②` | `no (narrowing)` duplicated the new entry's declaration. | `no`, true for what the note still states |
| `Skills-docs` | "stated here" would be false. | True: the rule is in the self-hosting docs |
| ADR-0087 marker | Tied to a breaking declaration the note no longer makes. | Removed. The new entry carries the disposition |
| BREAKING paragraph | False: it limited the rule to live mail. | True: it points at the new entry, which is pending for the same release |
| What changes, bullet 1 | False in two clauses. | True against `auth-manager-organization-plugin.ts:439-445` and the vendor route |
| What changes, bullet 2 | True | Unchanged |
| Who moves | Framed by the live-mail condition. | Removed. The new entry covers it |
| Unchanged | False | Removed. The new entry's "Unchanged" is true |
| `@objectstack/runtime` line | True | Unchanged |

Every sentence the note now carries is true at `bf3bf857d6`. `check-empty-changeset` is red on this file only, by design.

**Also judged**

- The four runtime pin suites change only their member-minting helper, which now goes through the operator door. No assertion moves.
- Docs: `environment-variables.mdx:100`, `tenancy-modes.mdx:246-249`, `authentication.mdx:125-128, 1213-1214` and `sso.mdx:751-754` are accurate against the code.
- New over-refusal: none found.

**Findings**

- **N5:** the body named `5147ad6a3a` as the final head. Fixed on this head: the body now carries the sync-merge note.
- **N6:** the request-scoped record depends on the vendor handing the same context object to the admission gate and both settle seams. The binding cases pin this today: 5 go red if the rule is disabled. A one-line comment naming them is suggested.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and correct:
- `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/verify` and `@object-ui/app-shell`;
- `Metadata-protocol: none`;
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, with the BREAKING banner, `!` and the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker on the new entry.

The corrected note is non-breaking at `patch` with plain `Clause-②: no`, so the release declares the narrowing once.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No governed path in this PR. The ADR amendment is #34909, which lands after or with this PR.
- The in-product no-mail hand-over is follow-up #34889.
- The sibling posture is a seat-owned follow-up.
- A residual on a neighbouring surface stays with the security seat. [detail held by the security seat]

### ④ Design judgment

The request-scoped record is the right shape. It mirrors `usersCreatedInRequest` and has no lifetime to tune. Policy-skip over bind-at-verification holds, as judged before. Reducing the superseded note, rather than deleting it, keeps its surviving attributions.

Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj`

**VERDICT: PASS**
